The '''2026 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the [[governor of Pennsylvania]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Josh Shapiro]] is seeking a second term. He is being challenged by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] state treasurer [[Stacy Garrity]].

[[Primary elections]] were held on May 19, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 26, 2025|title=2026 State Primary Election Dates|url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509222424/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2026-state-primary-election-dates|archive-date=May 9, 2026|access-date=September 27, 2025|website=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]}}</ref> Shapiro and Garrity secured their nominations unopposed. This is one of five Democratic-held governorships up for election in 2026 in a state that [[Donald Trump]] won in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]]. If elected, Garrity would be the first female governor of Pennsylvania.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Tannenbaum|first=Michael|date=August 15, 2025|title=Pa. Treasurer Stacy Garrity to run for governor against Josh Shapiro|url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/stacy-garrity-pennsylvania-governor-2026-republican-shapiro/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250818172457/https://www.phillyvoice.com/stacy-garrity-pennsylvania-governor-2026-republican-shapiro/|archive-date=August 18, 2025|access-date=May 25, 2026|work=Philly Voice}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[Pennsylvania]] is a [[purple state]] located in the [[Northeastern United States]]. A part of the [[Rust Belt]], it was narrowly won by Republican [[Donald Trump]] in [[2024 United States presidential election in Pennsylvania|his non-consecutive second victory in 2024]] after similarly narrow victories by Democrat [[Joe Biden]] in [[2020 United States presidential election in Pennsylvania|2020]] and Trump in his first election in [[2016 United States presidential election in Pennsylvania|2016]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/revisit-pennsylvania-election-results/|title=Revisit Pennsylvania election results from 2020 and 2016 ahead of Election Day 2024 - CBS News|date=November 4, 2024|website=www.cbsnews.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The 2024 presidential election was close, not a landslide |url=https://abcnews.go.com/538/2024-presidential-election-close-landslide/story?id=116240898 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241126224157/https://abcnews.go.com/538/2024-presidential-election-close-landslide/story?id=116240898 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 26, 2024 |website=ABC News}}</ref>

The state has a Democratic and Republican senator, making it one of only three states to have a split Senate delegation,{{efn|The other two are [[Maine]], with an independent who caucuses with the Democrats and a Republican, and [[Wisconsin]], with a Democrat and a Republican.<ref>[https://smartpolitics.lib.umn.edu/2024/11/19/119th-congress-smashes-record-low-for-number-of-split-us-senate-delegations/ 119th Congress Smashes Record Low for Number of Split US Senate Delegations], Smart Politics, November 19, 2024. Retrieved January 31, 2026</ref>}} while Republicans hold a majority in the state's House delegation, with ten seats to the Democrats' seven.<ref>{{cite news |title=119th Congress Smashes Record Low for Number of Split US Senate Delegations |url=https://smartpolitics.lib.umn.edu/2024/11/19/119th-congress-smashes-record-low-for-number-of-split-us-senate-delegations/ |access-date=September 4, 2025 |issue=Smart Politics |date=November 19, 2024}}</ref> Democrats also control the [[Pennsylvania House of Representatives]] while Republicans control the [[Pennsylvania Senate]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Democrats will again control Pennsylvania House after holding on to one-seat majority |url=https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2024/11/pennsylvania-election-results-2024-state-house-democratic-republican-control/ |access-date=September 4, 2025 |publisher=Spotlight PA |date=November 8, 2024}}</ref> 

Republicans have not won a Pennsylvania gubernatorial election since [[2010 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election|2010]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Josh Shapiro]] was first elected with 56.5% of the vote in  [[2022 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election|2022]], succeeding term-limited Democrat [[Tom Wolf]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/inside-josh-shapiros-2022-landslide-and-what-it-means-for-2024-analysis/|title=Inside Josh Shapiro's 2022 landslide -- and what it means for 2024 &#124; Analysis • Pennsylvania Capital-Star|first=Nick|last=Field|date=May 21, 2023}}</ref>

== Republican primary ==
=== Governor ===
Stacy Garrity was the only candidate on the ballot for the Republican nomination, making her the presumptive nominee. Supporters of [[2022 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election|previous nominee]] State Senator Doug Mastriano launched a write-in campaign, though Mastriano had previously stated he would not run for the nomination and had not expressed support for the campaign.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Downard |first1=Whitney |title=Sen. Doug Mastriano opts out of Pa. gubernatorial run in 2026 |url=https://penncapital-star.com/briefs/sen-doug-mastriano-opts-out-of-pa-gubernatorial-run-in-2026/ |website=Pennsylvania Capital-Star |date=January 7, 2026 |access-date=3 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ulrich |first1=Steve |title=Mastriano Supporters Embark On Write-In Campaign For Republican Gubernatorial Nomination |url=https://www.politicspa.com/mastriano-supporters-embark-on-write-in-campaign-for-republican-gubernatorial-nomination/146009/ |website=Politics PA |date=March 31, 2026 |access-date=3 April 2026}}</ref> Mastriano ultimately received 7,980 write-in votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Write-in Votes from May 19, 2026 Primary Election | website=Commonwealth of Pennsylvania |access-date=August 4, 2026 |ref={{harvid|Pennsylvania|2026}} |url=https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/dos/programs/voting-and-elections/running-for-office/2026/write-in%20votes_2026%20primary%20%20for%20website%20.pdf}}</ref>

==General election==
===Campaign===
A major issue in the general election has been the growing [[opposition to AI data centers]], similarly experienced throughout the country. Shapiro, despite having previously supported the construction of two [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] data center campuses estimated at $20 million the previous year and being quoted as saying Pennsylvania was "all in on AI",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cityandstatepa.com/policy/2026/05/gov-josh-shapiros-new-data-center-standards-reflect-new-reality/413789/|title=Gov. Josh Shapiro's new data center standards reflect new reality|first1=Justin|last1=Sweitzer|first2=Harrison|last2=Cann|website=[[City & State]]|date=May 27, 2026|access-date=August 27, 2026}}</ref> signed an executive order in August 2026 that implemented new regulations on them and eliminated fast-tracking of approvals to build them.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://whyy.org/articles/shapiro-data-centers-executive-order-pennsylvania/|title=Pennsylvania Gov. Shapiro signs wide-ranging executive order reining in data center development|first=Susan|last=Phillips|publisher=[[WHYY-TV]]|date=August 19, 2026|access-date=August 27, 2026}}</ref> Garrity has criticized Shapiro for this, claiming he "sold us out" for his prior support of Amazon's $20 million data center projects, although Garrity has similarly made comments supportive of AI data centers in the past and to which Shapiro has also capitalized on.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6055856-shapiro-garrity-pennsylvania-data-center-ads/|title=Shapiro, Garrity accuse each other of supporting data centers|first=Mira|last=Bhakta|website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|date=August 27, 2026|access-date=August 27, 2026}}</ref>
